dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Two parallel dome FSF pipelines now exist. (1) Script ratio: FSF = (H(r)/r)/(H(r_BOU)/r_BOU) per check_eclipse_fsf.py, version-dependent through H(r) and the station radii. (2) Locked page formula: FSF(lat) = 0.19550/sin(lat)^0.1640 x 32.974^(lat/90), a 3-constant fit in geographic latitude. Both feed delta_Z = baseline x coverage x FSF with two baselines (BOU -10.9 nT, W004 -22.24 nT). This run verified the published per-station predictions reproduce exactly (e.g., HAD -10.9*0.80*1.471 = -12.83 ~ published -12.8; LER -10.9*0.42*2.075 = -9.50 = published -9.5).
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: Hybrid, now with a third layer: the published FSF table is (a) hardcoded in predictions.html, (b) approximately reproducible from V51 dome radii (~3%), (c) near-exactly reproducible as tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) (<=0.0007 at 7/9 stations, this run's computation with INTERMAGNET latitudes and Boulder 40.015 N), and (d) fit by the locked FSF(lat) 3-knob formula (my RMSE 0.0117 with public latitudes vs dome-claimed 0.0071). (c) explains both (b) and (d): V51 radii approximately satisfy the Polaris equation r*tan(lat)=H(r), under which the dome parameters cancel algebraically out of the FSF ratio.

Our Part 2b.5/4.1 dashboard audit already catalogs it as FORM-V51-005 with three knobs, and EXP-283 froze the eclipse prediction, but the WIN panel — the surface the dome page itself tags '(WIN-044)' — has no answer. holes_found.description: UNRECONCILED CROSS-SURFACE TENSION + UNDERSOLD REPRODUCTION: WIN-044 says the published values 'reproduce to within ~3%' under V51 parameters and swing 28% under V50.6 — a version-instability frame. Section 4.2.4/4.2.5 and the analyst fingerprint carry the stronger and superficially OPPOSITE result: FSF reduces to tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) — dome-shape-INDEPENDENT, all dome parameters cancel — and this run verified the published table matches that pure tangent ratio to <=0.0007 at 7 of 9 stations (HAD 1.4706 vs 1.471, CLF 1.3240 vs 1.324, NGK/ESK/LER/COI/GUI within 0.0007; only EBR +0.005 and SPT -0.018 deviate, plausibly different station latitudes used). A defender can allege our review contradicts itself: 'version-unstable (WIN-044) or shape-independent (Section 4.2.4) — pick one.' The resolution is real but unstated in WIN-044: instability appears precisely when station radii are NOT re-derived from the Polaris equation (V50.6 city-fit radii -> HAD 1.894); when they ARE re-derived (V51), the formula collapses to globe trigonometry and 'reproduces' — by tautology, not by dome physics.
holes_found.recommendation: Add one bridging clause to detail_evidence and/or detail_verdict_text: 'the V51 reproduction succeeds only because V51 station radii are re-derived from the Polaris equation, under which FSF reduces to tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) — a globe-trigonometric identity in which every dome parameter cancels (see Section 4.2.4); the V50.6 failure shows what the formula does when its inputs are anything else.' This simultaneously resolves the apparent self-contradiction, answers the locked-formula defense (a 3-knob fit to a tangent ratio), and sharpens the Self-Contradicted verdict: the claimed V12 derivation outputs a number containing zero V12 information.

stronger_arguments.description: The tangent-ratio verification is the single strongest fact available and belongs in the WIN panel: the dome's published 9-station FSF table matches tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) (Boulder 40.015 N) to <=0.0007 at 7 of 9 stations — i.e., the 'V12 geometry' output is reproducible by anyone with a trig table and a list of globe latitudes, no dome required. This subsumes the ~3% V51 reproduction (V51 radii approximately satisfy the Polaris equation) and explains why the locked FSF(lat) fit works (it is a 3-knob approximation to a tangent ratio). The version-instability argument then slots in as the corollary: deviate from Polaris-equation radii (V50.6) and the 'derivation' swings 28%.

The dome's own page annotation is a self-own worth quoting verbatim: a formula 'independently derived from V12 geometry' that carries '[RMSE = 0.0071 across all 9 stations]' concedes in the same sentence that it was evaluated as a FIT against the nine numbers it supposedly derives. Derivations have proofs; fits have RMSEs.

advocate_mode.best_defense: As a dome defender accepting the review's own principles: 'You attack check_fsf.py and check_eclipse_fsf.py — exploratory scratch scripts — and call the model version-unstable. But the FSF Formula was LOCKED on 2026-03-22, before your EXP-165 citation pin (April 14) and your c4/c5 reviews, and it is the locked formula, not script archaeology, that the August 12 test will be scored against. Model refinement between V50.6 and V51 is normal science — general relativity's early metric forms changed too. The locked formula is stable, station-explicit, RMSE-quantified, and registered months before the eclipse. Your version-instability argument evaporates: there is exactly one prediction of record.'
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: The defense survives because WIN-044's text literally does not mention the locked formula — a reader cannot tell we know it exists. Neutralize with the H1 paragraph: the locked formula's sole input is globe latitude; its RMSE annotation is fit-language; its three constants have no published derivation; the lock date is unverifiable in the public git record (single commit 2026-04-05); and the tangent-ratio identity shows BOTH formulations output globe trigonometry with zero surviving dome content. Once that paragraph exists, the defense inverts into our strongest evidence: the dome answered 'your formula depends on dome version' by publishing a formula with no dome variables at all.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome author did something genuinely better than most of his WINs here: he registered nine station-specific, falsifiable numbers (raw-text/03-predictions.txt lines 26-34) before the event, with explicit coverage factors and tolerance bands, and then attempted to compress them into a closed-form scaling law (live predictions.html line 97, FSF(lat) with a stated RMSE). Publishing a quantified, station-resolved prediction table ahead of a dated natural experiment is real epistemic exposure — most WINs in this catalog never take that risk (cf. the post_hoc tag distribution in data/wins.json). The intuition that eclipse-day delta_Z varies systematically by station is also empirically respectable (WIN-068's Kim & Chang 2018 ensemble shows station-dependent amplitudes).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Exposure is not derivation. This run's computation shows the registered table is tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) to <=0.0007 at 7 of 9 stations (monitor/analyst/globe-fingerprints/WIN-044.json; verified against check_fsf.py fetched live) — the 'V12 geometry' content of the numbers is nil because the dome's own Polaris equation r*tan(lat)=H(r) cancels every dome parameter out of the FSF ratio. The locked FSF(lat) formula concedes the same point in its own annotation: '[RMSE = 0.0071 across all 9 stations]' (live predictions.html line 97) is goodness-of-fit language against the values it claims to derive. And the version-instability stands regardless: the same station produced FSF 1.894 under V50.6 inputs and 1.471 under V51 inputs (check_eclipse_fsf.py, check_fsf.py), so whatever the August data shows, 'derived from V12 geometry' (detail_claim) cannot be true of both parameter sets — which is the Self-Contradicted verdict (data/wins.json WIN-044 verdict field).

deeper_analysis: This cycle began as a routine punch-list verification and turned into a live-surface gap find. Verification first: all three c5 minors were cleanly applied — km units now consistent in both BOU radius mentions, the field-component symbol is now dZ, and 'primarily geometric' with the fitted-parameter caveat replaces 'purely geometric'. The claim retitle to 'Firmament Scaling Function from V12 geometry' accounts for the +15.8% claim_length drift. No regression in finding, detail_verdict_text, or either TLDR (lengths unchanged). One new minor was introduced by the fix itself: the dZ form is attributed to monitor.py line 515, which per our own EXP-165 pin reads dB = -18.22 x coverage x FSF — the symbol fix migrated the formula to the wrong source. The live fetch is where the cycle earned its keep. The dome's predictions page now carries a locked FSF(lat) formula tagged '(WIN-044)' — the dome is talking directly at this WIN's subject — and our panel does not acknowledge it. Quantitatively, everything in our text still checks out (every number re-verified, see quantitative_verification), but the argument's center of gravity has moved: the strongest available fact is no longer '28% between versions' but 'the registered table is globe trigonometry to four decimal places, and the dome's replacement formula is a three-knob fit to that trigonometry, annotated with its own RMSE'. The version-instability argument and the tautology argument must be explicitly bridged (Polaris-equation radii -> tautology; any other radii -> instability) or a defender will play them against each other. Timing discipline note: the lock label says 2026-03-22; the page's only git commit is 2026-04-05; our raw-text snapshot (2026-03-12) lacks the paragraph. I assert only what the public record shows — the label is unverifiable, which is itself the Timestamp Error pattern (anchoring claims on the mutable side). I deliberately do NOT claim the locked formula responds to our review: the 04-05 commit predates EXP-165 (04-14) and the c4/c5 cycles, and WIN-044's pre-April content was thinner. No responsiveness classification is warranted on the public evidence.
